starting_principles: Newton's second law for a particle: $\vec{F}_i = m_i \vec{a}_i$
Definition of torque for a particle: $\vec{\tau}_i = \vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_i$
Kinematics of rigid circular motion: $a_{i, \text{tan}} = r_i \alpha$
Newton's third law in strong form: internal forces are collinear with particle separation
assumptions: Rotation occurs about a fixed axis in an inertial reference frame.
All particles share a common angular acceleration $\alpha$.

ordered_steps.description: Discretize the rigid body into $N$ particles of mass $m_i$ rotating in planes perpendicular to the fixed axis $z$ at radial distances $r_i$.
ordered_steps.operation: Decompose the acceleration of each particle $i$ into tangential and radial components: $\vec{a}_i = a_{i, t} \hat{\theta}_i + a_{i, r} \hat{r}_i$, where $a_{i, t} = r_i \alpha$ and $a_{i, r} = -r_i \omega^2$.
assumptions_applied: Rigid body condition: all particles share identical angular velocity $\omega$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$.

ordered_steps.description: Apply Newton's second law along the tangential direction for particle $i$.
ordered_steps.operation: Multiply tangential acceleration by particle mass $m_i$ to find the net tangential force component acting on particle $i$: $F_{i, t} = m_i a_{i, t}$.
assumptions_applied: Newton's second law in an inertial reference frame.

ordered_steps.description: Calculate the axial component of torque $\tau_{i, z}$ acting on particle $i$ about the rotation axis.
ordered_steps.operation: Take the moment of force about the axis $z$: $\tau_{i, z} = r_i F_{i, t} = r_i (m_i r_i \alpha)$.
assumptions_applied: Radial force component passes through the axis and produces zero axial torque.

ordered_steps.description: Sum the torques over all constituent particles of the rigid body.
ordered_steps.operation: Sum both sides from $i=1$ to $N$ and factor out the common angular acceleration $\alpha$: $\tau_{\text{net}, z} = \sum_{i=1}^N \tau_{i, z} = \sum_{i=1}^N (m_i r_i^2 \alpha) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^N m_i r_i^2\right) \alpha$.
assumptions_applied: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is uniform across all elements of the rigid body.

ordered_steps.description: Demonstrate that internal torques between constituent particles cancel pairwise.
ordered_steps.operation: Decompose total torque into external and internal contributions: $\vec{\tau}_{\text{net}} = \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} + \sum_{i < j} (\vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_{ij} + \vec{r}_j \times \vec{F}_{ji}) = \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} + \sum_{i < j} (\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j) \times \vec{F}_{ij}$. By Newton's third law in strong form, $\vec{F}_{ij}$ acts along $(\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j)$, so $(\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j) \times \vec{F}_{ij} = \vec{0}$.
assumptions_applied: Newton's third law in strong (central force) form.

ordered_steps.description: Substitute the definition of moment of inertia $I = \sum_{i=1}^N m_i r_i^2$ (or $\int r_\perp^2 \, dm$) to finalize the equation.
ordered_steps.operation: Replace $\sum_{i=1}^N m_i r_i^2$ by the moment of inertia $I$.

applicability_conditions: Valid for rotation about a fixed axis in an inertial frame.
Valid about an axis passing through the center of mass even if the center of mass is accelerating.
Invalid for an accelerating non-CM point unless pseudo-force torque is included.
source_references: University Physics with Modern Physics, 13th Edition.pdf
